the use of a combination of a 3D-CTA and 2D-CTA in a patient with a LCA originating from the RCA, allowed the detection of a small thrombus in the proximal LAD, and that this was followed by a successful PCI.

the use of a novel, noninvasive method for measuring coronary flow reserve (CFR) in the right and left coronary artery systems is feasible and that CFR is significantly reduced in patients with coronary artery disease, especially those with multivessel disease.

the left coronary artery (LCA) originated from the right coronary sinus (RCS), and that a subacute myocardial injury (SMI) occurred in a patient with LCA originating from the RCS (LCAO) who was diagnosed with a myocardial infarct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship of the coronary arteries to each other, and to the aorta, and to the heart.
the management of a patient with left main coronary artery arising from the right coronary cusp.
the development of a novel method for the management of subacute myocardium infarction in patients with left coronary artery arising from the right coronary sinus.

the patient with a history of myocardial infarct should be treated with a statin.
the management of subacute MI in the presence of a left main coronary artery arising from the right coronary cusp is a challenging task.
the management of subacute myocardium infarction in patients with anomalous coronary artery origin is not clearly defined.

, the management of subacute myocardiac infarction in patients with left coronary artery (LCA) arising from the right coronary (RCA) is a rare and complex situation.
